A tagging-with-specific-tag is the type whose members are per-tag tagging headers — one per Tag, declaring how events are tagged as that Tag. Each member points at the Tag it is for via an a-tag (preferred) or an e-tag. The member has no target, so the a/e slot is free for the Tag reference (unlike a tagging assertion, where a/e holds the target and the Tag is reached indirectly via a z-tag).

A nostr-event-tag is an event that applies a specific Tag to a specific event (referenced by the e or a tag). The descriptor (which Tag) is referenced indirectly via a z-tag pointing at the Tag's per-tag tagging header, leaving e/a free for the target. Optional polarity is expressed as an event-tag (1 = applied, -1 = disputed; absent = applied). Publishing is permissionless; whether a tagging counts is computed per point-of-view at read time.

A tag-pinning is an assertion by a nostr user that they personally pin a specific tag — i.e., they opt that tag into their personal curated set, to be used as the basis for downstream features such as periodic Trusted List publication (Story 12) and 'most pinned' aggregation (Story 13). Each element links the pinning user (event author) to a tag event id and carries a curation-method describing how the user wants the eventual Trusted List computed. Pinning is permissionless: any user may pin any tag; unpinning is performed by publishing a NIP-09 kind-5 deletion targeting the pin event.

The word-wrapper is Tapestry's canonical JSON format for the 'json' tag of any core node or firmware concept event. It has two sections: (1) a universal 'word' key with slug, name, title, wordTypes array, and coreMemberOf array; (2) one or more type-specific keys (conceptHeader, superset, set, property, primaryProperty, graph, conceptGraph, coreNodesGraph, propertyTreeGraph) containing the node's structured data. A Web of Trust (WoT) is a decentralized reputation system where trust propagates through human relationships rather than central authorities. In Nostr, WoT is derived from follow lists (kind 3) and mute lists (kind 10000): users you follow are implicitly trusted, and their follows extend trust transitively. In Tapestry, WoT (via GrapeRank) determines which concept definitions achieve 'loose consensus' across the community.
